chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira and others, who said:

Hamza ibn Humran married the daughter of Bukayr. When it was the night she was brought to him, the women said to him, 'You do not care about divorce, and it is not with anything in your presence, and we will not let her come to you until you perform Dhahar from the mothers of your children.' He said, so he did it. He mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he ordered him to go near them.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: Refers to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أُدْخِلَ بِهَا: He was brought to her: Refers to the night of consummation (dakhala biha).
key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِ أَوْلَادِكَ: Mothers of your children: The phrase used in the formula of Dhahar.
key_terms.ظَهَار: Dhahar: A form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence where a husband likens his wife's back to his mother's back.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Dhahar when performed with the intention of preventing divorce or as a social custom, according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of Dhahar by Hamza ibn Humran, who, advised by women to avoid immediate divorce, likened his wife to his mother. Upon reporting to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Imam’s directive to consummate the marriage underscores that Dhahar does not sever the marital bond but rather suspends sexual relations until the expiation (Kaffarah) is performed, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. The incident illustrates the flexibility of the ruling in cases where the husband seeks to maintain the marriage without formal divorce.
